subject: Tenant multiplexing, scaling scenarios and link budget for private VPC GPU pool
messages:
From: Alex Jansen <alex.jansen@telcoinc.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Park <sam.park@telcoinc.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 17:01:00 -0700
Subject: Multiplexed tenant scaling & throughput targets for private VPC GPU pool

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for taking this in the RFP. We're starting internal sizing for a private VPC deployment and need to align on the throughput and network allowances you can guarantee. High-level requirements:

- Workload profile: mix of synchronous chat (avg 120 tokens/request) and async batch reranking.
- Expected steady state: ~1.8M tokens/hour (across our prod tenancy).
- Peak burst: up to 3.6M tokens/hour sustained for 30 minute windows during events.
- Concurrency target: 1.2k concurrent requests (median payload sizes as above).
- Latency requirement: p95 <= 400ms for chat requests under normal load.

We're particularly worried about two operational cliffs: cold KV-cache warmup for repeated prompts, and network egress during burst windows (we operate in three regions, starting with US). Can you provide:

1) A proposed capacity profile (pods, GPUs per pod, expected tokens/hr per pod) for baseline and burst
2) Link budget and egress numbers per pod so our network team can provision peering/bandwidth
3) A short mutual action plan for staging + acceptance tests (what metrics you'll guarantee during soak)

Procurement is cc'd and will want any commitments in the MAP.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if easier.

Alex
Director of Edge Platforms
TelcoInc
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jansen <alex.jansen@telcoinc.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multiplexed tenant scaling & throughput targets for private VPC GPU pool

Alex —

Appreciate the clear numbers. Summary answers up front and an attachment with a first-pass model attached (telco_headroom_model_v1.xlsx) plus a short warmup/playbook (warmup_playbook.pdf).

Short answers:
- Capacity profile (initial proposal): three pod classes:
  * Baseline pod: 4xA800 GPUs, optimized quantized FP16 path — ~1.2M tokens/hr per pod steady state for mixed chat+rerank.
  * Burst pod: identical pod configuration but admitted only during event windows; can scale to 4 pods for short bursts (~4.8M tokens/hr combined).
  * Staging pod(s): mirrored smaller fleet for acceptance tests (2xA800).
- Headroom: we recommend a 25% headroom on top of your peak to allow KV cache warmup and transient admission control. See attached headroom model for math.
- Network: expect ~1.1–1.4 Gbps egress per active 4-GPU pod during heavy token emission (estimates in model). Peering + 10% buffer recommended.

Operational notes and mitigations:
- KV-cache warmup: pre-warm the top 500 frequent request prefixes during a 15–30 minute ramp; warmup_playbook.pdf includes tooling hooks we can run from your staging cluster.
- Admission control: we'll propose a two-level policy (soft throttles at 80% of target; hard rejects at 100% of provisioned concurrency) to preserve p95 SLAs.
- Multiplexing: we can partition tenants into two multiplex pools to limit noisy-neighbor impacts — details in the model.

Next steps:
1) Internal technical review with your SREs (Jonas and Karthik are cc'd) — propose Tue 4/6 10:00 PT.
2) We run a tailored staging soak (48h) with your pilot traffic; acceptance criteria listed in MAP draft.
3) Agreement on reserved capacity and MAP terms (procurement/path will be included).

I've attached the model and warmup playbook. If the numbers look broadly correct we'll iterate with your team and add a network budget CSV for your network team.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- telco_headroom_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- warmup_playbook.pdf (pdf)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alex Jansen <alex.jansen@telcoinc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multiplexed tenant scaling & throughput targets for private VPC GPU pool

Alex / Irene —

Adding technical detail from the runtime side so your SREs can budget correctly. Attached: pod_network_budget.csv with per-pod link estimates. Key items:

- Kernel and perf: we'll run quantized FP16 with our optimized attention kernels for chat; throughput numbers assume little packing loss (prefetch and batching enabled).
- Per-pod throughput: ~1.2M tokens/hr for mixed chat + rerank on a 4xA800 pod (sustained). During bursts, with multiplexing and continuous batching we see near-linear scaling until backend memory pressure forces lower batch sizes.
- Headroom math: reserve 15% for runtime/system overhead + 10% conservative buffer (total ~25%).
- Network budget: average 0.95 Gbps idle emission rising to 1.35 Gbps during token-dense responses (long completions). Planning number: 1.4 Gbps outbound per active 4-GPU pod.
- Admission control thresholds: suggest soft throttle at 0.7 * provisioned concurrency and hard at 0.95. We can tune after staging.

I've attached the CSV for your network team. Happy to run a quick readout with your networking leads and map peering options (direct connect, transit).

-Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachment: pod_network_budget.csv
From: Alex Jansen <alex.jansen@telcoinc.com>

Subject: Re: Multiplexed tenant scaling & throughput targets for private VPC GPU pool

Irene / Jonas —

Thanks for the headroom model and the network budget. A couple follow-ups from procurement and SRE:

- Procurement needs an estimate for monthly reserved capacity price for the baseline (steady 1.8M tokens/hr) and the burst posture (ability to scale to 3.6M tokens/hr for two 30-minute windows per week). Can you give a ballpark monthly cost or point us to the pricing tiers used for Dedicated/Private?
- SRE wants a formal staging test plan (we need pass/fail criteria to sign off). Can you provide the step-by-step soak and the metric cutoffs (throughput sustained, p95 latency, error rates)?
- If we proceed we'll need a draft MAP to attach to our internal approval flow. Procurement is ready to review a 30/60/90 day plan and acceptance signoffs.

Procurement (procurement@telcoinc.com) — cc'd — will handle the contractual side; Samuel (cc'd) will own the staging target environment details.

Alex

Subject: Re: Multiplexed tenant scaling & throughput targets for private VPC GPU pool

Alex / Procurement / Samuel —

Linked a short MAP draft and put acceptance criteria below. I've also attached MAP_TelcoInc_v1.docx to this thread; once you confirm we will push a DocuSign draft (link above).

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Week 0: Technical kickoff and network peering checklist (we validate egress and route tables).
- Week 1: Deploy mirrored staging pods (2x4-GPU) and run smoke tests.
- Week 2: 48-hour soak at expected steady 1.8M tokens/hr. Acceptance: sustained throughput within +/-10% of target and p95 latency <= 400ms for chat with error rate <0.5%.
- Week 3: Controlled burst tests: two 30-minute bursts to 3.6M tokens/hr with KV-cache pre-warm. Acceptance: p95 <= 450ms during burst, no systemic errors, and no eviction-induced failures.
- Week 4: Final signoff and cutover plan for production reserved capacity.

SLA / Pricing notes (ballpark until MAP is finalized):
- SLA class: Standard reserved (p95 latency target as above, 99.5% availability for provisioned pods).
- Pricing: ballpark monthly reserved fee for baseline capacity (equivalent to 2x 4-GPU pods reserved) + on-demand burst usage billed at a premium. Vanessa will follow up with a formal quote.
